claims.text: The as-cast CrMnFeCoNi alloy is initially single phase.
Standard casting produces a homogeneous CrMnFeCoNi solid solution with uniformly distributed elements.
The as-cast alloy has clean grain boundaries without significant nanosegregation.
The as-cast CrMnFeCoNi alloy has a high level of ductility.
Isothermal annealing at 400–500 °C induces grain-boundary nanosegregation in initially single-phase CrMnFeCoNi.
Cr, Ni, and Mn are among the elements that segregate to grain boundaries during intermediate-temperature annealing.
Thermal exposure during annealing drives stress-assisted diffusion.
Annealing-driven diffusion forms nanoscale clusters or compositionally enriched zones at grain boundaries.
Grain-boundary nanosegregation reduces grain-boundary cohesive strength.
Reduced grain-boundary cohesion predisposes CrMnFeCoNi to intergranular brittle fracture under mechanical loading.
The local grain-boundary compositional modification triggers a transition from ductile behavior to brittle failure under mechanical load.
Annealed specimens will have lower fracture strain than as-cast specimens.
Annealed specimens will exhibit earlier onset of intergranular cracking than as-cast specimens.
Annealed specimens will exhibit statistically significant grain-boundary nanosegregation relative to as-cast specimens.
The proposed embrittlement mechanism applies under moderate-temperature service and mechanical loading.
The proposed mechanism may not apply at extreme temperatures or strain rates.
The proposed mechanism may not transfer to alloy systems outside the CrMnFeCoNi family.

contradictions.description: The mechanism invokes stress-assisted diffusion during annealing, but the annealing intervention specifies no applied stress; mechanical loading is introduced only during subsequent testing. Thus the source and timing of the claimed stress assistance are internally unresolved.
